data.title: Who is Raul John Aju, the 'AI Kid of India' who met Russian Prez Putin?
data.description:
Kerala-based teenager Raul John Aju, who goes by the moniker the ‘AI Kid of India’, is going viral on social media after sharing a selfie with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
 
“From making my first video in a bathroom at 9 to taking a selfie with President Putin, never in my wildest dreams did I think life would take me here,” Aju wrote in his Instagram post.
 
“Meeting some incredible people at AI Journey (way smarter than me) made me realise how much more I have to learn,” he added.
 

Who is Raul John Aju?

 
Aju is a young entrepreneur, developer and content creator who has earned the nickname ‘AI Kid of India’ for his early interest in technology.
 
 
At 12, Aju reportedly developed his first humanoid robot, marking an early milestone in his journey as a technology enthusiast.
 
 
 
 
View this post on Instagram
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

A post shared by Raul John Aju (@raul_the_rockstar)

By 16, Aju had ventured into entrepreneurship, founding AIRealm Technologies Pvt Ltd in August 2024. He serves as the company's founder and chief technology officer (CTO). According to his LinkedIn profile, the company is developing a legal technology platform that aims to provide users with instant legal guidance.

data.title: SAP flags security incident, says no evidence of customer data breach
data.description:
SAP "has identified suspicious activity" but found no evidence so far ‌of unauthorized access to its customer business data, the  German software firm told Reuters on Friday.
 
In a statement, SAP said it promptly implemented ‌the necessary measures to protect its customers and preserve the security of its services after ‌identifying the activity.
 
"Based ‌on our investigation to ‌date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data," it said.
 
Spiegel magazine reported on Thursday ‌a cyberattack at the company, ‌citing an internal memo to staff.

data.title: Sensex tanks 780 pts intraday after 2-day rise: Consolidation here to stay?
data.description:
Stock market crash today: The benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty 50 pulled back after a two-day rally as oil prices extended their rise, and investors took some profits off the table following sharp gains seen this month. 
 
BSE barometer Sensex lost 781 points or 0.92 per cent to hit an intraday low of 83,547. Its NSE counterpart Nifty 50 declined 218 points or 0.84 per cent to 25,666.75. 
 

What's behind the market decline today?

The decline in the indices comes on the back of 4 major triggers:
 
1. Oil prices spike
Crude oil prices advanced amid escalating supply-side risks in West Asia, including tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and concerns over potential disruptions to Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure. These developments have heightened concerns over crude oil exports and regional supply stability.
 
 
At the last check, Brent crude futures were up 0.8 per cent at $97.33 a barrel. In the context of rising inflation in India, hardening of crude prices is negative news. 
 
2. Profit taking
The sharp rise seen this month also paved the way for profit taking ahead of key policy events in December. The indices remain over 12 per cent higher for the month despite these pullbacks, with the market exhibiting resilience mainly through sustained FII buying, supported by improving fundamentals.
 
3. Rate hikes likely
Investors also adopted a cautious stance in light of the possible interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
US October PCE inflation rose to 3.8 per cent, while Q3 GDP growth was revised upwards to 4.3 per cent. This combination has reinforced expectations of a further 25bp Fed rate hike in December, said Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services. On the domestic front, India’s Q2FY27 GDP estimates due on Monday and the RBI’s monetary policy decision on Friday, 4 December, will be closely watched, he added. 
ALSO READ: Gold, silver prices extend rebound on strong buying at lower levels
 
4. Technical view
PL Capital said that the technical parameters for Nifty are positioned at their highly overbought zone and the chances of some profit booking cannot be ruled out with some cooling off process required, having the near-term support at 25,200 level while the major support is positioned near the 24,800 level which needs to be sustained.
 
Meanwhile, for Sensex, the near-term support is at 81500 zone which needs to be sustained whereas, on the upside, the index would have the resistance zone near the 86,000 level which if decisively breached shall trigger for a breakout and expect for further rise in the coming days. CHECK Stock Market LIVE Updates 

Market consolidation here to stay?

Analysts believe that in the context of these above headwinds, there is no room for a sustained rally in the market.
 
Dr VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments, said a consolidation phase appears likely in the near-term.
 
Hitesh Tailor, technical research analyst at Choice Broking, also believes that mixed global cues and resistance near key psychological levels may restrict immediate upside.
 
"Banking stocks and broader market participation will be important in determining whether the recent consolidation develops into another upward move or extends into a wider trading range," he noted.

data.title: MCX market cap hits ₹1 trillion; stock rallies 11% in two days, up 77% YTD
data.description:
Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) share price movement

 
Share price of Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) extended its up move, hitting a new high of ₹3,939.85, gaining 3 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intraday deals amid an otherwise weak market. In the past two trading days, the stock price of the exchange and data platform company rallied 11 per cent on healthy business outlook. 
 
Thus far in the calendar year 2026, MCX’s market price surged 77 per cent compared to a 1.8 per cent decline in the BSE Sensex. It more than doubled or zoomed 102 per cent from its 52-week low of ₹1,948.67 touched on December 11, 2025.
 
 
Amid the sharp rally, MCX hit the ₹1 trillion market capitalisation mark for the first time in intraday deals on Friday.
 
At 12:15 PM, with a ₹99,976 crore market capitalisation, MCX quoted 2 per cent higher at ₹3,920.75 on the BSE, data shows. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was down 0.70 per cent at 83,741.
 

Why has MCX outperformed the market?

 
The MCX is India’s leading Commodity Derivatives Exchange and the largest Commodity Options Exchange globally. MCX has a market share of over 98 per cent in terms of the value of commodity futures contracts traded in April to September 2026 (H1FY27). It offers trading in a diverse range of commodities, spanning multiple segments including bullion, energy, metals and agri commodities, as well as sectoral commodity indices. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex slumps 600 pts, Nifty tests 25,700; Nifty IT down 1%
 
MCX's operating revenue is up 2x year to date (YTD) in FY27, led by a similar increase in options average daily turnover (ADTO) (75 per cent of MCX's operating revenues). 
 
The ADTO grew to ₹12.6 trillion, up 20 per cent from the last quarter at ₹10 trillion and nearly double what MCX saw the same quarter last year. This reflects a wider adoption of commodity derivatives by market participants as well as improved liquidity, the company said in its Q2 earnings conference call.
 
MCX is emerging as a clear structural beneficiary of India’s deepening commodity derivatives ecosystem. The company remains well placed to benefit from sustained growth in commodity derivatives, supported by rising participation, increasing financialization of commodities, and healthy bullion trading volumes. 
 
According to analysts at Jefferies, India’s commodity market lags cash equities, but penetration should rise, with MCX, the leading non-agri exchange, well-placed to benefit.
 
MCX's revenue could grow at 25 per cent compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over FY26-29e despite the elevated base, noting new product scope and retail participation being only 1/5th of the National Stock Exchange (NSE's). Along with 140bps margin expansion, profit before tax CAGR could be 26 per cent to FY29e, the brokerage firm said. Jefferies has a ‘Buy’ rating on MCX stock with a target price of ₹4,300 per share.
 
“We have increased our fair multiple to 45x Dec'28E EPS, higher than the 31x/35x fair multiples for BSE/NSE, given MCX's room to expand its penetration and product offerings, as well as optionality,” analysts at Jefferies said. It forecasst MCX's revenue to grow at a c.25 per cent 3-year revenue/profit after tax CAGR through FY29e, factoring in commodity options share increases to c.15 per cent of equity options, up from 8 per cent in FY26. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Centre urges states to sign 41 GW of pending clean power contracts
data.description:
India's federal government urged states on Friday to sign more contracts for 41 ​gigawatts (GW) of clean energy capacity that ​has no buyers.

States need to identify their power ‌requirements well in advance and sign more battery storage contracts along with clean energy, Shripad Naik, union minister of state for power and new and renewable energy, said at the State Power Ministers Conference in New Delhi.

The lack of battery energy storage resulted in states scrambling for power to meet their evening and ‌night demand as the El Nino weather pattern pushed up consumption this year.

The unexpected surge in demand strained India's power system in September and October despite the country having surplus solar energy, Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal said at the conference.

 

Peak ​power demand of 271 GW in May was 11.6% higher than ‌a year earlier, Agarwal said.

"There were days we could barely meet their evening peak ​demand ‌despite having surplus clean energy during the day," Agarwal said.

Naik also urged states to speed up payments tied to the acquisition of land for transmission ‌projects, ​saying slow payments ​have led to huge delays.

Insufficient transmission capacity has forced India to curtail renewable power ‌generation, which ​has wasted clean energy.

data.title: Swiggy's Instamart lays off 340 employees amid wider AI adoption push
data.description:
Instamart, Swiggy's quick commerce arm, has laid off around 340 employees as part of a restructuring exercise, amid increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and efforts to streamline operations, Moneycontrol reported on Friday.
 
The job cuts have primarily affected employees in corporate and support functions within Instamart, the report said. The restructuring comes as the company faces intensifying competition in the quick commerce market and continues to report losses.
 
Swiggy has yet to respond to the report.

Instamart faces mounting losses and competition

The reported layoffs come as Instamart continues to face pressure from rivals, including Eternal-owned Blinkit, Zepto, Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now.
 
 
In the September quarter, Instamart's adjusted Ebidta loss widened to ₹895 crore from ₹778 crore in the previous quarter.
 
Swiggy's financial results, declared on October 22, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, showed that Instamart's adjusted Ebidta margin improved to -9.7 per cent from -9.8 per cent in the June quarter. The quick commerce business reported an overall loss of ₹895 crore during the September quarter.
 
Instamart's net order value grew 13.4 per cent sequentially to ₹6,594 crore. The company added 69 dark stores during the quarter, taking its total network to 1,240 stores across the country.

Nandita Sinha takes charge of Instamart

The restructuring is the first major development under Instamart's new chief executive officer, Nandita Sinha, who took charge on August 3, succeeding Amitesh Jha.
 
Sinha previously served as the chief executive officer of Myntra.
 
Instamart has also been changing its business strategy, with a greater focus on private-label products. The company recently introduced Noice for snacks and beverages and Nectr for fresh fruits and vegetables, according to The Economic Times.
 
In its October 22 earnings release, Swiggy CEO Sriharsha Majety outlined the company's approach to competition in quick commerce.
 
"We see assortment as a curation game rather than a volume game, and our aim is to enable consumers to buy better, not just offer more," Majety said. 
ALSO READ: Last day to buy Tech Mahindra shares for bonus eligibility: Key details

Swiggy plans shift to inventory-led model

Swiggy is also preparing to move Instamart towards an inventory-led business model following its transition to an Indian-owned and controlled company (IOCC).
 
In its letter to shareholders accompanying the September quarter results, the company said the transition to the inventory-led model would begin in mid-Q3 FY27 and take two to three quarters to complete, The Economic Times reported.
 
The shift is expected to give Swiggy greater control over inventory, pricing and product availability as it seeks to strengthen Instamart's operations, the report said. 
ALSO READ: Apple removes Chinese AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns

data.title: Samay Raina makes YouTube history with 1 million paid channel members
data.description:
Indian comedian Samay Raina has become the first YouTube creator globally to cross one million channel members, setting a new record on the platform. YouTube confirmed the feat and shared it in a post on the Google India blog. 
 
The achievement comes as Raina rebuilds his career following the controversy surrounding India's Got Latent in February 2025.
 
Raina currently has more than 12.4 million subscribers on YouTube. However, the one-million milestone refers to paid channel memberships, through which viewers financially support creators in exchange for exclusive content and other benefits.

Youtube on Samay Raina’s one million milestone

Praising Samay's journey, the YouTube team mentioned, “From host-level banter with Grandmasters to creating the phenomenon that is India's Got Latent, Samay turned his YouTube channel into the ultimate virtual hangout for millions.”
 
 
It added, “Samay's 1-million-channel-member landmark captures a much bigger cultural moment happening across India right now. Audiences aren't just watching from the sidelines anymore; they're choosing to show up for their favourite creators in deeply personal, meaningful ways. In June 2026 alone, more than 1.2 million fans in India bought at least one channel membership on YouTube, driving a 25%+ year-over-year jump in membership revenue for Indian creators.”
 
The platform also emphasised the increasing trend of paid channel memberships among creators in India. “It's an extraordinary moment for Samay and a proud moment for India's entire creator ecosystem. Congratulations, Samay! We can't wait to see what hilarious, high-energy concept you bring to life next,” the post added.

Samay Raina’s comeback

Raina's latest achievement follows a turbulent phase in his career after India's Got Latent became embroiled in controversy in February 2025. This situation resulted in multiple police filings and FIRs against various individuals connected to the specific episode. 
 
In response, Samay Raina issued an apology and deleted all episodes from the initial season on his YouTube channel. He made a comeback in 2026 with his stand-up special Still Alive, where he spoke about the “difficult period”. Eventually, he reintroduced India's Got Latent with a season 2, which debuted on both YouTube and Netflix.
 
Samay said, "I was depressed when we were in Canada. I used to ask ChatGPT, ‘When do you think Samay Raina will ever be able to bring his show back?’ ChatGPT would reply, ‘It's unclear right now’. Then I used to write, ‘Please say yes.’ I had no idea that the show would come back in this manner." 
ALSO READ: Hanuman Ansh OTT release: When and where to watch spiritual biopic online?

Who is Samay Raina?

Samay Raina is an Indian stand-up comedian, YouTuber and chess enthusiast. He rose to prominence after winning the second season of the comedy reality show Comicstaan, alongside Aakash Gupta.
 
He later gained widespread popularity through his YouTube content, chess streams and comedy talent show India's Got Latent, which became one of the most talked-about digital shows in India. 
ALSO READ: 27-year-old Jennifer Barreto from Puerto Rico crowned Miss Universe 2026

data.title: Sebi looking into Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal, says minority interests key
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is looking into the proposed Tata Steel-APL Apollo transaction, with protection of minority shareholders remaining a key priority for the regulator, Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Friday.
 
“We take minority shareholders’ rights very seriously. Investor protection is very important,” Pandey told journalists on the sidelines of Assocham’s 17th Capital Markets Conference.
 
The regulator is yet to receive the revised contours of the proposed transaction after Tata Steel publicly indicated that it would re-examine the structure. Under takeover regulations, the draft offer document is ordinarily required to be filed within five working days of the public announcement. Sebi is expected to wait for the revised proposal before proceeding further.
 
 
The regulator’s comments come after institutional investors and proxy advisory firms raised concerns over the proposed transaction, prompting Tata Steel Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer T V Narendran to assure investors that the structure would be reviewed.
 
The proposed transaction involves Tata Steel acquiring a controlling stake in APL Apollo Tubes while APL Apollo acquires Tata Steel’s downstream tubes and colour-coated steel businesses.
 
Under the announced structure, Tata Steel agreed to acquire a 26.6 per cent promoter stake in APL Apollo for ₹15,510 crore and make an open offer for another 26 per cent at ₹2,301.40 per share, involving a maximum consideration of ₹16,756 crore.
 
APL Apollo, meanwhile, would acquire Tata Steel’s downstream businesses — including its tubes division, Khopoli unit and Tata Steel Colors — for ₹28,000 crore.
 
Tata Steel has already acquired around 9.91 per cent of APL Apollo through a block deal at ₹2,100 per share for approximately ₹5,825 crore.
 
The proposed transaction has faced scrutiny from institutional investors and proxy advisory firms over the valuation assigned to the businesses being transferred, the financing burden on APL Apollo and safeguards for its minority shareholders.
 
The concern centres on the simultaneous nature of the transaction: APL Apollo is expected to acquire Tata Steel’s downstream assets while Tata Steel becomes its controlling shareholder.
 
Investors have questioned whether the structure adequately protects minority shareholders as the ownership and capital structure of APL Apollo changes.
 
Pandey’s remarks indicate that Sebi is closely monitoring these issues, even as it awaits the revised transaction structure from the companies.
 
The overall transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and had earlier been targeted for completion by March 2027.

data.title: Inside the Tata Sons power struggle: The rules, the rift and the road ahead
data.description:
The battle to lead India's Tata Sons, the owner of marquee brands such as Jaguar Land Rover and Tetley Tea, headed for court on Friday after the sprawling conglomerate flouted the wishes of its controlling charity arm to reappoint ​the chairman.

Tata Trusts holds a stake of 66% in Tata Sons, but the latter's board re-appointed chairman ​N. Chandrasekaran and has decided to pursue a possible stock market listing, putting the power struggle at the centre of the standoff.

It is the ‌second such fight in a decade for one of India's oldest and most reputed business houses, after a years-long legal battle over Tata Sons' decision to remove earlier chairman Cyrus Mistry ended in the Supreme Court upholding the decision.

 

Here is how the current fight could play out, along with views of both sides and the complex structures, according to people familiar with the matter:

TRUSTS WANT CHANDRASEKARAN OUT OF KEY DECISIONS

Two of the seven charitable trusts that control Tata Sons asked the Mumbai high court on Thursday to declare Chandrasekaran's reappointment 'invalid, illegal, null and void', copies of internal memos reviewed by Reuters showed.

They also seek court directions that key decisions by Tata Sons require complete support from the charity arm.

Reuters has learnt the trusts will tell the court that the board should not have proceeded with the decision as both trust nominees did not back the chairman's reappointment.

At Friday's hearing, the trusts are expected to ask for a halt to plans for a November 30 board meeting set to decide next steps towards listing if the chief of the charity arm ‌and family head Noel Tata, as trust nominee, does not vote in favour.

The board of Tata Sons agrees to the stock market listing, ordered by the central bank, but the charity arm does not.

COURT CASE FOLLOWS BITTER PUBLIC DEBATE

Both sides have hired top lawyers to defend them and explain who can call the shots.

Lawmaker and Congress party leader Abhishek Manu Singhvi is representing the Tata Trusts led by Noel Tata.

Singhvi has previously said the dispute is about shareholder supremacy and the conglomerate cannot act like a "runaway board" independent of the controlling shareholder.

That position is disputed by Tata Group's Chandrasekaran, who has roped in Harish Salve, a former solicitor general of India who often represented the government in global forums.

In television remarks Salve has said the board's decision was in line with internal governing rules, urging the charity ​arm to get past the "I control the trusts, I control this group mindset."

WHY CAN'T THE TRUSTS CALL A SHAREHOLDER MEETING AND OUST THE CHAIRMAN?

The Tata Trusts ‌have problems of their own that weaken their influence. Formed of several affiliated charities, they could have used their voting power to call for a shareholders' meeting to effectively oust Chandrasekaran.

But a regulator has barred one of the main charities, the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, from convening its own meetings ​in a dispute over internal ‌appointments.

In turn, internal rules mean the charities currently lack the power to call for a meeting of Tata Sons shareholders.

The trusts can either wait for the deadlock to ‌lift, once the regulatory inquiry ends, or ask a court to lift the curbs, two people familiar with the matter said.

COURT FIGHT CENTRES ON 'ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION'

At the heart of the dispute facing the court is the Tata Sons' governance framework known as the "articles of association", since Tata Trusts and Tata Sons ‌disagree on ​the interpretation of ​thee rules, which are not public.

The charity arm says Noel Tata's opposition to the reappointment was sufficient to halt the decision. It believes such decisions cannot be made in the absence of support of a majority of the trusts' two board nominees.

In this case, "majority amongst two is ‌two and not one," the charity ​arm has publicly argued.

Tata Sons' lawyer Salve disagrees, saying both trust nominees voted differently, prompting a casting vote that helped reappoint the chairman under the governance rules.

data.title: Sebi takes minority shareholders' rights seriously: Chairman Tuhin Pandey
data.description:
Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Friday said the market regulator takes minority shareholders' interests very seriously and supports the role of proxy advisory firms in flagging governance concerns.

Investor protection remains one of Sebi's key priorities, Pandey said.

When asked about the Tata Steel-APL Apollo Tubes proposed deal, he said proxy advisory firms have every right to raise issues concerning minority shareholders, adding that public discussions and media scrutiny of such concerns are welcome.

"Minority shareholders' interest is very important to us. Proxy advisers have every right to bring issues to the fore. They represent minority shareholders, and we support them when they raise such concerns. Investor protection is one of the most important things for us," Pandey said on the sidelines of an event here.

 

The remarks come amid concerns raised by proxy advisory firms over the deal's structure, valuation, and protection of APL Apollo's minority shareholders.

Tata Steel on Monday said it has executed an agreement to acquire the entire 26.6 per cent promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd for Rs 15,510 crore and plans to take over another 26 per cent in the pipes and tubes maker through an open offer of Rs 16,756 crore, a move that will increase the Tata group firm's downstream production capabilities three times.
